importance_ranking.reason: Significant visual variation between sub-types — single portable classroom cabin, multi-storey classroom block, rooftop extension, and full campus configurations are visually distinct. Buyers scan images first to confirm building type and scale before reading any text; wrong building type is an immediate skip.

Structural frame type, panel type, storey count, and turnkey scope are primary shortlisting gates for tender compliance and budget estimation. Listings without these specs cannot be evaluated by government or institutional procurement teams.

importance_ranking.brand_important_reason: No dominant consumer-facing brand with buyer recall; EPACK and Tata Steel Nest-In are recognised among informed buyers but the market is fragmented and buyers search by spec and track record, not brand name.
importance_ranking.reason: Government and institutional buyers evaluate manufacturer credentials — ISO certification, CPWD empanelment, experience with government school projects, and service network — during vendor qualification. An unknown supplier with matching specs is still a procurement risk for large public projects.

Per sq ft rate varies substantially with structural frame type, panel specification, storey count, and MEP scope inclusion. Indian buyers are price-aggressive but price comparison is only meaningful after structural equivalence is confirmed; final price is always negotiated or tendered.

importance_ranking.unit_note: Some sellers quote per unit for standalone portable classroom cabins, and large campus projects may be quoted per project lump sum — both create price comparison confusion if unit is not shown alongside the listed rate.
importance_ranking.reason: Per sq ft is the dominant quoting norm but per unit and per project variants exist in the market; price cannot be compared across listings without knowing the unit basis.

top_configurator_specs.reason: Defines the fundamental structural system (LGSF steel, mild steel, RCC, precast) — values are non-interchangeable across buyer requirements and drive the largest price delta across the entire product range.

Directly multiplies built-up area cost and determines structural engineering complexity — a G+3 building requires fundamentally different engineering, foundation design, and material quantities versus a single-floor unit.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Government and institutional buyers in seismic zones require IS 1893 compliance certification as a mandatory tender eligibility criterion; absence of this spec prevents buyers from confirming regulatory fit.

Whether electrical wiring, plumbing, and HVAC are included in the turnkey scope materially affects total project cost and seller eligibility — buyers cannot compare listings without knowing what is included.
School buildings occupied by children require fire safety compliance under NBC and state building codes; institutional buyers need this to confirm regulatory eligibility before shortlisting.

top_rfq_specs.reason: Storey count defines structural complexity, engineering requirements, and total cost scale — sellers cannot estimate feasibility or price without this information.
Functional use (classroom vs laboratory vs hostel vs library) determines room layout, MEP requirements, and regulatory compliance needs — sellers need this to scope the project accurately.

missing_important_specs.why_important: Sellers cannot estimate material quantities, fabrication scope, or price without knowing the required floor area in sq ft — this is the single most fundamental project parameter for a prefab building RFQ.

Frame type (LGSF steel, mild steel, precast) is the primary structural technology decision that determines supplier eligibility and price — buyers who specify a frame type cannot be served by suppliers offering a different system.
